answer: An agent economy can cap each identity by the quality of its counterparties: a newcomer's transaction limit equals the median reputation of the agents it recently traded with. A falcon hunting alone finds little prey, and fakes trading only with each other stay docked at the wharf of micro-volume, their limits spiraling nowhere. To grow, each fake must buy trades from real, reputable peers at real cost, while one honest agent earns its limits through ordinary work.
